backward_compat_traps.rule: Both ends must use the same subclass (0/1/2) for deterministic latency to work.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Mixing a Subclass 1 (SYSREF) end with a Subclass 0 end loses deterministic latency.
A 204C-only (64b/66b) link cannot interoperate with a 204B (8b/10b) link unless the device is dual-mode.

backward_compat_traps.rule: L/M/F/S/N/N'/K/SCR must match at both ends (verified by FCHK).
backward_compat_traps.trap: A mismatch fails the ILAS FCHK check and the link will not enter the data phase.

backward_compat_traps.rule: SYNC~ is active-low (assert = 0) and is the RX->TX request in 204B.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Treating SYNC~ as active-high inverts the bring-up handshake.

backward_compat_traps.rule: The lane clock is embedded (recovered by CDR); the Device Clock is a separate shared reference.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Assuming a forwarded/source-synchronous lane clock (as in DDR or UCIe) is wrong for JESD204.

backward_compat_traps.rule: SCR must be the same at both ends.
backward_compat_traps.trap: One end scrambling while the other does not yields garbage data.

fields.ic_name: JESD204 Serial Interface for Data Converters (JESD204B/C)
fields.spec_version: JEDEC JESD204B (July 2011) and JESD204C (December 2017), Serial Interface for Data Converters
previous_versions: JESD204 (2006) — single lane, up to 3.125 Gbps, no lane alignment.
JESD204A (2008) — multiple lanes + multi-lane alignment, up to 3.125 Gbps.

key_changes.summary: Up to 12.5 Gbps/lane, 8b/10b coding, deterministic latency via Subclass 0/1/2 (SYSREF/SYNC~), CGS+ILAS bring-up, LMFC/multiframe alignment, optional scrambling (1+x^14+x^15), the L/M/F/S/N/N'/K parameter set.

Up to 32 Gbps/lane; 64b/66b (optional 64b/80b) link layer (~97% efficiency) replacing 8b/10b; sync-header block / multiblock alignment; optional Reed-Solomon FEC; in-band command channel; deterministic latency via SYSREF retained; dual-mode interop with 204B.

future_versions_industry_outline.summary: Higher lane rates and 128b/132b-class coding under discussion at JEDEC; same converter-link model.

fields.version_naming_history_note: JESD204 is maintained by the JEDEC JC-16 Committee. JESD204 (2006) introduced the single-lane converter serial link; JESD204A (2008) added multi-lane alignment; JESD204B (2011) added deterministic latency (subclasses, SYSREF/SYNC~), 8b/10b, and up to 12.5 Gbps; JESD204C (2017) added the 64b/66b link layer, optional FEC, the command channel, and up to 32 Gbps. Facts here are grounded in the public JEDEC JESD204B/JESD204C standards.
